item.title: Golang Deep Dive: Concurrency, Runtime & Architecture
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: In-depth technical notes on Go concurrency, memory management, garbage collection internals, performance profiling, hexagonal architecture, and design patterns. Concurrency & Channels Channel Types 1. Unbuffered Channel Behavior: An unbuffered channel has zero capacity (make(chan int)). Synchronization: Requires both sender and receiver to be ready at the exact same moment. Send blocks until a receiver is ready, and receive blocks until a sender is ready. Use Case: Strict point-to-point synchronization between goroutines.

item.title: Linux & Operating System Internals
item.author: ThanhLD
item.description: Operating System Internals & Linux Table of Contents Processes Process Concept Process States & Types Threads Process vs Thread Context Switching Memory Management (Stack vs Heap, Virtual Memory) Cron & Scheduling Storage & Mount Disk Essential Linux Troubleshooting Commands Processes Process Concept A running instance of a program is called a process and it runs in its own memory space. Each time you execute a command, a new process starts. An active process also includes the resources the program needs to run.
